analysis.evidence: In אֶת קַשְׁתִּי נָתַתִּי בֶּעָנָן, God places his bow in the cloud. The cloud is where the bow appears, and the bow serves as the sign of the covenant.
analysis.morphology: בֶּ combines the preposition בְּ with the definite article before עָנָן, a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: God sets his bow in the cloud and says וְהָיְתָה לְאוֹת בְּרִית, “and it shall serve as a sign of the covenant.” The bow is the visible sign of the covenant between God and the earth.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ marks the role the bow will serve. אוֹת is a common noun of common gender, singular in the construct state, linked to בְּרִית.

analysis.evidence: God sets his bow in the cloud as the sign of a covenant described as בֵּינִי וּבֵין הָאָרֶץ, “between me and the earth.” The bow identifies this as the covenant with Noah and all flesh.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the absolute state, with no prefix or suffix. It completes the construct phrase לְאוֹת בְּרִית, “as a sign of a covenant.”
analysis.sense: the covenant with Noah and all flesh
